blurb: Week 0 is the first day of your last period. There is no baby yet — dating starts here because it is the one date that can be pinned down reliably.
looks: No baby yet; this is the start of the count.

blurb: Still counting from your last period. Ovulation is roughly a fortnight away.
looks: No baby yet; the body is preparing for ovulation.

blurb: Ovulation happens around now. Conception, when it happens, is usually dated to this week.
looks: No baby yet; an egg is released around now.

blurb: A fertilised egg is dividing as it travels to the uterus and implants. Far too small to see.
looks: A tiny ball of cells, far too small to see, with no features yet.

blurb: Implantation is complete and the pregnancy hormone hCG starts rising — this is when a test usually turns positive.
looks: A flat disc of cells in layers, which will go on to form every part of the body.

blurb: The neural tube, which becomes the brain and spinal cord, is forming. The heart is a simple tube that has just begun to beat.
looks: A curved, tadpole-like shape with a tiny beating heart tube and dark spots where the eyes will be.

blurb: Facial features start as small folds. Arm and leg buds appear. A heartbeat may be visible on an early scan.
looks: A small curled shape with a head, a tail and tiny buds where the arms and legs will grow.

blurb: The brain is growing fast. Hands and feet look like paddles. The umbilical cord is fully formed.
looks: The head is large compared with the body, and the arm buds are flattening into paddles.

blurb: All the essential organs have begun to form. Fingers and toes are webbed but distinct.
looks: Fingers and toes are starting to show as ridges on the paddles, and the tail is fading.

blurb: The embryo is officially a fetus this week. Tiny muscles allow the first movements, far too faint to feel.
looks: A recognisable small person shape, with eyelids beginning to form and the toes distinct.

blurb: Vital organs are in place and starting to work. Nails begin forming and bones are hardening.
looks: The tail is gone, fingers and toes are separate, and the skin is thin and see-through.

blurb: The head is still about half the total length. Tooth buds are appearing and fingers and toes have separated.
looks: The head is about half the length of the body, and the eyelids have closed over the eyes.

blurb: Reflexes are developing — fingers can curl. The 12-week dating scan usually happens around now.
looks: The face looks more human, with a nose, chin and ears in place, and tiny nail beds starting.

blurb: Start of the second trimester. Vocal cords are forming and fingerprints have appeared.
looks: The skin is translucent enough to show blood vessels, and the eyelids stay fused shut.

blurb: The baby can squint, frown and grimace. Fine downy hair called lanugo covers the body.
looks: Fine downy hair called lanugo begins to cover the skin, and the neck is longer.

blurb: Bones are hardening quickly. The baby can sense light through closed eyelids.
looks: Eyebrows and scalp hair start to appear, and the skin is still thin and see-through.

blurb: Facial muscles allow expressions. The heart pumps around 25 litres of blood a day.
looks: The ears stand out a little from the head, and fingernails are forming.

blurb: Fat stores begin forming under the skin. The skeleton is shifting from cartilage to bone.
looks: The first fat starts to build under the skin, which is still thin and wrinkled.

blurb: Hearing is developing — the baby may start to register sounds. Many people feel the first movements around now.
looks: The ears are in their final position, and the fingers have their own tiny prints.

blurb: A waxy coating called vernix now protects the skin. The senses are developing rapidly.
looks: A creamy coating called vernix begins to cover the skin, with lanugo holding it in place.

blurb: Halfway. The anomaly scan usually happens this week. From next week length is measured crown to heel, so the number jumps.
looks: Covered in vernix and fine lanugo, with eyebrows, lashes and fingernails all visible.

blurb: Measurement switches to full length, crown to heel. The baby swallows small amounts of amniotic fluid daily.
looks: Lean and long with thin, reddish, wrinkled skin; the eyebrows and eyelids are well formed.

blurb: Eyebrows and eyelashes are visible. Grip is developing and the sense of touch is sharpening.
looks: The face looks like a miniature newborn's, though the lips and eyebrows are still faint.

blurb: Hearing is good enough to pick up your voice. Skin is still wrinkled while fat fills out underneath.
looks: The skin is wrinkled and red-tinged, with fingernails reaching the fingertips.

blurb: A milestone week: lungs are developing the branches needed to breathe air.
looks: The skin is translucent and wrinkly, and the face is fully formed with eyelashes in place.

blurb: The baby is putting on fat steadily. Hair is growing and beginning to show colour and texture.
looks: The body is filling out a little and the skin is starting to look smoother, with hair growing thicker.

blurb: Eyes open for the first time. Lungs are practising breathing movements with amniotic fluid.
looks: The eyelids begin to open, and the eyes are formed.

blurb: End of the second trimester. Sleeping and waking patterns are becoming regular and hiccups are common.
looks: The eyes open and close, and the eyelashes are fully grown.

blurb: Third trimester. The brain is developing deep grooves and the baby can now dream.
looks: The skin is less see-through as more fat builds up, and the head is covered in hair.

blurb: Muscles and lungs are maturing. Kicks are getting noticeably stronger.
looks: The body is plumper and the skin is becoming smoother and pinker.

blurb: Around a litre and a half of amniotic fluid surrounds the baby — this begins to reduce as space runs short.
looks: The lanugo is starting to thin out, and the skin is smoother as the fat layer grows.

blurb: All five senses are working. The baby is putting on weight quickly now.
looks: Rounder in shape, with fingernails reaching the tips and skin that is no longer see-through.

blurb: Fingernails and toenails have grown in. Most babies have turned head-down or will soon.
looks: The toenails are in place and the skin is pink and smooth.

blurb: Skull bones stay soft and separate to make the journey out easier. The immune system is developing.
looks: The skin is soft and smooth as the fat layer thickens, and the head hair is growing.

blurb: Fat continues to fill out under the skin. Lungs are nearly ready.
looks: Covered in a thick coat of vernix, with fingernails reaching past the fingertips.

blurb: The brain gains weight rapidly. Space is tight, so movements feel more like rolls than kicks.
looks: Plump and rounded, with most of the lanugo gone and the skin soft and smooth.

blurb: The baby is likely head-down and settling into position. Weight gain is around 30g a day.
looks: The wrinkles smooth out as fat fills in, and the body looks like a newborn's.

blurb: Early term. The baby practises breathing, sucking and blinking, getting ready for the outside.
looks: Fully formed, with a thick vernix coat and soft skin; hair length varies a lot from baby to baby.

blurb: Organs are mature and ready. The vernix and lanugo are mostly shed.
looks: The lanugo has mostly gone, and the vernix is thinning, with firm, smooth skin.

blurb: Full term. The chest is becoming more prominent and the head is roughly the size of the chest.
looks: Plump and smooth, with a layer of fat under the skin and nails that may need trimming at birth.

blurb: Your due date. Only about 4 in 100 babies arrive on it — anywhere from 37 to 42 weeks is normal.
looks: A full-term newborn look, with smooth skin, a rounded body and often a little vernix left.
